newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK, Japan sign air services agreement - HK Govt. [CORRECTED 06:40 GMT]
newsitem.headline: HK, Japan sign air services agreement - HK Govt. [CORRECTED 06:40 GMT]

text.p: Hong Kong and Japan signed an air services agreement on Friday after eight years of negotiation, the Hong Kong government said.
The deal, signed by Hong Kong's Economic Services Secretary Stephen Ip and Japanese Consul-General Hideaki Ueda, was approved by China last November, it said in a statement.
Beijing's permission was needed as the accord straddles the British colony's return to Chinese sovereignty on July 1.
The agreement was modelled very closely on the current British arrangements concluded in 1986, the statement said.

Japan is a major market for all three of Hong Kong's airlines -- Cathay Pacific Airways Ltd, Hong Kong Dragon Airlines (Dragonair) and cargo carrier Air Hong Kong Ltd, a 75 percent held subsidiary of Cathay Pacific.

Dragonair is 36 percent owned by mainland state owned China National Aviation Corp, while Swire Pacific and Cathay Pacific, a Swire unit, together hold about 26 percent. CITIC Pacific Ltd holds 28 percent of Dragonair (corrects ownership).
In 1996, the Japanese market represented about 18 percent of the total revenue earned by the three Hong Kong carriers, the government statement said.

Japan Airlines Co Ltd, All Nippon Airways Co Ltd, Japan Air System Co Ltd and the three Hong Kong airlines together carry some four million passengers each year, serving nine cities in Japan, it said.
The Hong Kong-Japan agreement is the 16th air services agreement signed by Hong Kong.
The others were signed with the Netherlands, Switzerland, Canada, Brunei, France, New Zealand, Malaysia, Brazil, Sri Lanka, Australia, Germany, South Korea, Singapore, Italy and India.
